source.anchor_kjv: …they shake the head, saying, He trusted on the LORD that he would deliver him: let him deliver him…
source.thread: Psalm 22:7-8, written ~1000 years early, records the mockers' GESTURE (shaking the head) and their TAUNT ('let him deliver him'); at the cross the crowd did exactly both — Matthew 27:39 wagging their heads and 27:43 sneering 'let him deliver him now' — the mockers unknowingly reciting the prophecy that marks Him as the One.
source.thread_lever: NT-confirmed OT echo (predictive correspondence, undisputed text both sides)
source.hook_line: At the cross they shook their heads and sneered the very taunt a psalm had recorded a thousand years before, psalm 22.
source.spoken_script: At the cross they shook their heads and sneered the very taunt a psalm had recorded a thousand years before, psalm 22. David, describing a mocked and dying man, even writes his tormentors words. They shake the head, saying, he trusted on the Lord that he would deliver him, let him deliver him. A thousand years later, at the cross, Matthew records both. The passers-by wagging their heads, and the religious leaders jeering. He trusted in God, let him deliver him now. The same gesture, the same taunt, flung at him by people who never saw what they were echoing. Let him deliver him, they sneered. And he wasn't delivered, not because Jesus lacked the power to come down, he had every power. He stayed because staying was the only way to deliver you. They thought weakness pinned him to that cross. It was love. He could have come down in an instant. He chose to stay with you in view.

platforms.description:
At the cross they shook their heads and sneered a taunt — one a psalm had recorded a thousand years earlier.

Psalm 22:7-8 (KJV): "they shake the head, saying, He trusted on the LORD that he would deliver him: let him deliver him."

Matthew 27 records both: the wagging heads (v.39) and the exact taunt — "let him deliver him now" (v.43). Same gesture. Same words. A millennium apart.

They thought they were mocking a failed messiah. They were unknowingly reciting the prophecy that marked Him as the One.

He could have come down. He chose to stay — not from weakness, but because staying was the only way to deliver you.

platforms.label: YouTube (Long-form 16:9)
platforms.title: Psalm 22 Wrote the Mockers' Words 1,000 Years Before the Cross
platforms.description:
At the cross, the crowd shook their heads and sneered: "He trusted in God — let him deliver him now." They thought they were improvising a taunt. They were reciting a psalm written a thousand years before they were born.

Psalm 22:7-8 (KJV): "they shake the head, saying, He trusted on the LORD that he would deliver him: let him deliver him."

David wasn't writing a song about himself. He was recording a scene he hadn't witnessed yet — the gesture (wagging the head), the specific taunt, the exact words. Then in Matthew 27:39 and 27:43, both appear at the cross, word for word.

The mockers thought they were exposing a fraud. They were authenticating the Messiah.

He had every power to come down. He stayed — because staying was the only way to deliver you. That's not weakness. That's the love the cross was always about.

Psalm 22 | Matthew 27 | KJV

redteam:
VERDICT: REVISE

Two real problems; rest is clean.

1. **YouTube Short / YouTube Long description — "exact taunt" + partial Matthew quote.**
   The descriptions call "let him deliver him now" the "exact taunt" (YT Short) and quote Matthew 27:43 accurately in substance — but Matthew 27:43 KJV reads in full: "He trusted in God; let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of God." Calling a truncated rendering "exact" is a precision failure. A skeptic WILL clip this. Fix: drop "exact" → "the same taunt" OR extend the Matthew quote to show the fuller correspondence. The Psalm 22 → Matthew parallel is real and undisputed; don't weaken it with a precision error.

2. **YouTube Long description — "David wasn't writing a song about himself."**
   Psalm 22 IS a Davidic lament (headed "A Psalm of David" — context a reader will know); it's read as simultaneously Davidic AND messianic. Flatly stating David wasn't writing about himself is a slight overclaim that a careful reader will dispute and that invites a "debunking" comment thread. Fix: "David was writing more than a personal lament — he recorded a scene he couldn't have witnessed" or simply let the correspondence stand without the negative claim.

Everything else is solid:
- KJV quotes are verbatim in all three platforms that carry them (YouTube Short, YouTube Long, Facebook). ✓
- TikTok hook ("At the cross they shook their heads…") is punchy and accurate as a first line. ✓
- The thread (gesture + taunt, Psalm 22:7-8 → Matt 27:39,43) is consistently carried across platforms. ✓
- No gain/loss or fear framing; CTA is grace-anchored ("He chose to stay… because staying was the only way to deliver you"). ✓
- No composer names, no "official audio" language, no ToS landmines. ✓
- Hashtag mix is appropriate and not spammy. ✓
- Instagram/TikTok correctly have no title. ✓

Minimum fix to pass: (1) Change "exact taunt" → "same taunt" in YT Short and YT Long descriptions. (2) Soften the "David wasn't writing about himself" line in YT Long.
